extracted.intended_audience: investigators/authors reporting randomized clinical trials of interventions involving AI (and journal editors/peer reviewers assessing such reports)
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting-extension checklist and explanatory guidance for randomized controlled trials that evaluate interventions with an AI/ML component, intended to ensure transparency and completeness of trial reports. Targets manuscript elements (title/abstract, methods, results, other information) with AI-specific reporting items.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT-AI 1a,b (i) — Indicate AI/ML in title/abstract and specify model type
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate that the intervention involves artificial intelligence/machine learning in the title and/or abstract and specify the type of model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicating in the title and/or abstract that the intervention involves AI/ML facilitates identification, indexing and searching. Use a broader umbrella term (e.g., 'artificial intelligence' or 'machine learning') in the title so it is understandable to a wide audience; reserve more precise model-type terminology for the abstract unless the term is widely recognized. Specific terminology relating to the model type and architecture should be detailed in the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT-AI 1a,b (ii) — State intended use in title/abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: State the intended use of the AI intervention within the trial in the title and/or abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the intended use of the AI intervention in the context of the clinical pathway, including its purpose and disease context. Because intended use may evolve or be multiple, documenting it allows readers to understand the purpose for which the algorithm was evaluated at the time of the trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT-AI 2a (i) — Explain intended use in clinical pathway
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the intended use for the AI intervention in the context of the clinical pathway, including its purpose and its intended users (for example, healthcare professionals, patients, public).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a detailed description of the AI's role in the clinical pathway in the background section of the report. Clarify whether the AI is replacing, augmenting or adjudicating components of clinical decision-making and who the intended users are, as this helps readers understand the purpose and applicability of the evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT-AI 4a (i) — Participant-level inclusion/exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: State the inclusion and exclusion criteria at the level of participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define participant eligibility as per usual practice for non-AI trials. Distinguish these participant-level criteria from input-data-level criteria (addressed in 4a (ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT-AI 4a (ii) — Input-data-level inclusion/exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: State the inclusion and exclusion criteria at the level of the input data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Input data’ refers to the data required by the AI intervention (for example, unprocessed images, physiologic measurements). Pre-specify minimum requirements for input data (e.g., image resolution, quality metrics, data format) that determine pre-randomization eligibility and specify when, how and by whom this was assessed. If input data are acquired after randomization, state that any exclusion is from the analysis (not enrollment), and report accordingly (CONSORT item 13b). Provide examples such as excluding a participant because the scan quality was inadequate for AI use.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT-AI 4b — Describe integration into trial setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how the AI intervention was integrated into the trial setting, including any onsite or offsite requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide details of hardware and software requirements to enable technical integration at each study site (e.g., vendor-specific devices, specialized computing hardware, cloud integration). State if changes to the algorithm were required at sites (for example, fine-tuning on local data) and describe those processes. This information is important because AI algorithms’ performance can depend on operational/development environment and affects generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT-AI 5 (i) — Specify algorithm version used
rubrics_metrics.description: State which version of the AI algorithm was used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because AI systems often undergo multiple iterations, report the exact version used in the trial, whether it is the same as versions used in prior supporting studies, and whether the version changed during the trial. Describe what changed between versions and rationales for changes. Where available, include regulatory marking references (e.g., unique device identifier) that distinguish updated versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT-AI 5 (ii) — Describe acquisition and selection of input data
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how the input data were acquired and selected for the AI intervention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain input-data handling including acquisition, selection and pre-processing performed before analysis by the AI system. Provide enough detail for replicability and to allow readers to assess whether input-data-handling procedures were standardized across trial sites. Note that measured performance may depend critically on nature and quality of input data.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT-AI 5 (iii) — Handling of poor-quality or unavailable input data
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how poor-quality or unavailable input data were assessed and handled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the amount of missing data and how it was identified and handled. Specify any minimum standard required for input data and, where standards were not achieved, how this was managed (including any impact on participant care pathways). If input-data exclusion criteria differ from pre-randomization eligibility, state this. Report similar information for comparator/control interventions where relevant. Provide examples (e.g., movement artifact on ECG making input unusable).

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT-AI 5 (iv) — Human–AI interaction and required user expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify whether there was human–AI interaction in the handling of the input data, and what level of expertise was required of users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the human–AI interface and requirements for successful interaction when handling input data (for example, clinician selection of regions of interest). Describe any user training provided and instructions for handling input data to ensure transparency and replicability. Clarify whether errors are attributable to human deviation versus AI failure, since poor clarity on the interface can have ethical implications and affect interpretation of harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT-AI 5 (v) — Specify AI intervention output
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the output of the AI intervention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state the nature of the AI output (e.g., diagnostic classification, probability, recommended action, alarm, class-activation map, or automated action in a closed-loop system). The output type has direct implications for usability and downstream actions and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT-AI 5 (vi) — Explain how outputs contributed to decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the AI intervention’s outputs contributed to decision-making or other elements of clinical practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how humans used the AI outputs to make decisions, including downstream interventions affecting outcomes, the level of expertise needed to interpret outputs, training/instructions given, intended thresholds for action (example: excision if probability >80%), and how comparator interventions produced and used information. Report any discrepancies between intended decision pathways (per protocol) and how decision-making actually occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT-AI 19 — Analysis and reporting of performance errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe results of any analysis of performance errors and how errors were identified, where applicable. If no such analysis was planned or done, justify why not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report performance errors and failure-case analyses because AI systems can make unforeseen errors that may have serious consequences if deployed at scale. Describe how errors were identified, present results of performance-error analyses, discuss implications for safety and for which populations and settings the intervention may be safely implemented, and describe risk-mitigation strategies. If none conducted, explain rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT-AI 25 — Accessibility of the AI intervention and/or code
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether and how the AI intervention and/or its code can be accessed, including any restrictions to access or re-use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear whether and how the AI intervention or its source code is available for access or reuse; include details about licensing and any restrictions. This information supports reproducibility and assessment of the intervention.
